context: Write the truth values of the following statements.
stem: All flowers are red or all cows are black.
solution:
Let \(p\) : All flowers are red ; \(q\) : All cows are black.
Truth values of p and q are F and F respectively.
The given statement in the symbolic form is \(p \vee q\)
\(\therefore p \vee q \equiv F \vee F\) is F
\(\therefore\) Truth value of given statement is F.

solution:

\(\therefore p \to q \equiv T \to T\) is T

context: Write the truth values of the following statements.
stem: Milk is white if and only if the Sun rises in the West.
solution:
Let \(p\) : Milk is white; \(q\) : Sun rises in the West.
Truth values of p and q are T and F respectively.
The given statement in symbolic form is \(p \leftrightarrow q\)
\(\therefore p \leftrightarrow q \equiv T \leftrightarrow F\) is F
\(\therefore\) Truth value of given statement is F.

context: If statements p, q are true and r, s are false, determine the truth values of the following.
solution:
\(\sim p \wedge (q \vee \sim r) \equiv \sim T \wedge (T \vee \sim F) \equiv F \wedge (T \vee T) \equiv F \wedge T \equiv F\)
Hence truth value is F.

context: If statements p, q are true and r, s are false, determine the truth values of the following.
solution:
\((p \wedge \sim r) \wedge (\sim q \vee s) \equiv (T \wedge \sim F) \wedge (\sim T \vee F) \equiv (T \wedge T) \wedge (F \vee F) \equiv T \wedge F \equiv F\)
Hence truth value is F.

context: If statements p, q are true and r, s are false, determine the truth values of the following.
solution:
\([\sim (p \to q)] \leftrightarrow (r \wedge s) \equiv [\sim (T \to T)] \leftrightarrow (F \wedge F) \equiv (\sim T) \leftrightarrow (F) \equiv F \leftrightarrow F \equiv T\)
Hence truth value is T.

context: If statements p, q are true and r, s are false, determine the truth values of the following.
solution:
\((\sim p \to q) \wedge (r \leftrightarrow s) \equiv (\sim T \to T) \wedge (F \leftrightarrow F) \equiv (F \to T) \wedge T \equiv T \wedge T \equiv T\)
Hence truth value is T.

stem:
Construct the truth table for each of the following statement patterns.
i) \(p \to (q \to p)\)
ii) \((\sim p \vee q) \leftrightarrow \sim (p \wedge q)\)
iii) \(\sim (\sim p \wedge \sim q) \vee q\)
iv) \([(p \wedge q) \vee r] \wedge [\sim r \vee (p \wedge q)]\)
v) \([(\sim p \vee q) \wedge (q \to r)] \to (p \to r)\)
solution:
i) \(p \to (q \to p)\)

| \(p\) | \(q\) | \(q \to p\) | \(p \to (q \to p)\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | T | T |
| T | F | T | T |
| F | T | F | T |
| F | F | T | T |

ii) \((\sim p \vee q) \leftrightarrow \sim (p \wedge q)\)

| \(p\) | \(q\) | \(\sim p\) | \(\sim p \vee q\) | \(p \wedge q\) | \(\sim (p \wedge q)\) | \((\sim p \vee q) \leftrightarrow \sim (p \wedge q)\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | F | T | T | F | F |
| T | F | F | F | F | T | F |
| F | T | T | T | F | T | T |
| F | F | T | T | F | T | T |

iii) \(\sim (\sim p \wedge \sim q) \vee q\)

| \(p\) | \(q\) | \(\sim p\) | \(\sim q\) | \(\sim p \wedge \sim q\) | \(\sim (\sim p \wedge \sim q)\) | \(\sim (\sim p \wedge \sim q) \vee q\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | F | F | F | T | T |
| T | F | F | T | F | T | T |
| F | T | T | F | F | T | T |
| F | F | T | T | T | F | F |

iv) \([(p \wedge q) \vee r] \wedge [\sim r \vee (p \wedge q)]\)

| \(p\) | \(q\) | \(r\) | \(\sim r\) | \(p \wedge q\) | \((p \wedge q) \vee r\) | \(\sim r \vee (p \wedge q)\) | \([(p \wedge q) \vee r] \wedge [\sim r \vee (p \wedge q)]\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | T | F | T | T | T | T |
| T | T | F | T | T | T | T | T |
| T | F | T | F | F | T | F | F |
| T | F | F | T | F | F | T | F |
| F | T | T | F | F | T | F | F |
| F | T | F | T | F | F | T | F |
| F | F | T | F | F | T | F | F |
| F | F | F | T | F | F | T | F |

v) \([(\sim p \vee q) \wedge (q \to r)] \to (p \to r)\)

| \(p\) | \(q\) | \(r\) | \(\sim p\) | \(\sim p \vee q\) | \(q \to r\) | \(p \to r\) | \((\sim p \vee q) \wedge (q \to r)\) | \([(\sim p \vee q) \wedge (q \to r)] \to (p \to r)\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | T | F | T | T | T | T | T |
| T | T | F | F | T | F | F | F | T |
| T | F | T | F | F | T | T | F | T |
| T | F | F | F | F | T | F | F | T |
| F | T | T | T | T | T | T | T | T |
| F | T | F | T | T | F | T | F | T |
| F | F | T | T | T | T | T | T | T |
| F | F | F | T | T | T | T | T | T |

subtopic: Logical Equivalence and Algebra of Statements
stem:
Using truth tables, prove the following logical equivalences.
i) \((p \wedge q) \equiv \sim (p \to \sim q)\)
ii) \((p \leftrightarrow q) \equiv (p \wedge q) \vee (\sim p \wedge \sim q)\)
iii) \((p \wedge q) \to r \equiv p \to (q \to r)\)
iv) \(p \to (q \vee r) \equiv (p \to q) \vee (p \to r)\)
solution:
i) \((p \wedge q) \equiv \sim (p \to \sim q)\)

| \(p\) | \(q\) | \(\sim q\) | \(p \wedge q\) | \(p \to \sim q\) | \(\sim (p \to \sim q)\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | F | T | F | T |
| T | F | T | F | T | F |
| F | T | F | F | T | F |
| F | F | T | F | T | F |

Columns (IV) and (VI) are identical \(\therefore (p \wedge q) \equiv \sim (p \to \sim q)\)

ii) \((p \leftrightarrow q) \equiv (p \wedge q) \vee (\sim p \wedge \sim q)\)

| \(p\) | \(q\) | \(\sim p\) | \(\sim q\) | \(p \leftrightarrow q\) | \(p \wedge q\) | \(\sim p \wedge \sim q\) | \((p \wedge q) \vee (\sim p \wedge \sim q)\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | F | F | T | T | F | T |
| T | F | F | T | F | F | F | F |
| F | T | T | F | F | F | F | F |
| F | F | T | T | T | F | T | T |

Columns V and VIII are identical \(\therefore (p \leftrightarrow q) \equiv (p \wedge q) \vee (\sim p \wedge \sim q)\)

iii) \((p \wedge q) \to r \equiv p \to (q \to r)\)

| \(p\) | \(q\) | \(r\) | \(p \wedge q\) | \((p \wedge q) \to r\) | \(q \to r\) | \(p \to (q \to r)\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | T | T | T | T | T |
| T | T | F | T | F | F | F |
| T | F | T | F | T | T | T |
| T | F | F | F | T | T | T |
| F | T | T | F | T | T | T |
| F | T | F | F | T | F | T |
| F | F | T | F | T | T | T |
| F | F | F | F | T | T | T |

Column (V) and (VII) are identical \(\therefore (p \wedge q) \to r \equiv p \to (q \to r)\)

iv) \(p \to (q \vee r) \equiv (p \to q) \vee (p \to r)\)

| \(p\) | \(q\) | \(r\) | \(q \vee r\) | \(p \to (q \vee r)\) | \(p \to q\) | \(p \to r\) | \((p \to q) \vee (p \to r)\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | T | T | T | T | T | T |
| T | T | F | T | T | T | F | T |
| T | F | T | T | T | F | T | T |
| T | F | F | F | F | F | F | F |
| F | T | T | T | T | T | T | T |
| F | T | F | T | T | T | T | T |
| F | F | T | T | T | T | T | T |
| F | F | F | F | T | T | T | T |

Columns V and VIII are identical \(\therefore p \to (q \vee r) \equiv (p \to q) \vee (p \to r)\)

stem:
Using truth tables, examine whether each of the following statement pattern is a tautology or a contradiction or contingency.
i) \((p \wedge q) \wedge (\sim p \vee \sim q)\)
ii) \([p \wedge (p \to \sim q)] \to q\)
iii) \((p \to q) \wedge [(q \to r) \to (p \to r)]\)
iv) \([(p \vee q) \vee r] \leftrightarrow [p \vee (q \vee r)]\)
solution:
i) \((p \wedge q) \wedge (\sim p \vee \sim q)\)

| \(p\) | \(q\) | \(\sim p\) | \(\sim q\) | \(p \wedge q\) | \(\sim p \vee \sim q\) | \((p \wedge q) \wedge (\sim p \vee \sim q)\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | F | F | T | F | F |
| T | F | F | T | F | T | F |
| F | T | T | F | F | T | F |
| F | F | T | T | F | T | F |

All the truth values in the last column are F. Hence it is contradiction.

ii) \([p \wedge (p \to \sim q)] \to q\)

| \(p\) | \(q\) | \(\sim q\) | \(p \to \sim q\) | \(p \wedge (p \to \sim q)\) | \(p \wedge (p \to \sim q) \to q\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | F | F | F | T |
| T | F | T | T | T | F |
| F | T | F | T | F | T |
| F | F | T | T | F | T |

Truth values in the last column are not identical. Hence it is contingency.

iii) \((p \to q) \wedge [(q \to r) \to (p \to r)]\)

| \(p\) | \(q\) | \(r\) | \(p \to q\) | \(q \to r\) | \(p \to r\) | \((q \to r) \to (p \to r)\) | \((p \to q) \wedge (q \to r) \to (p \to r)\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | T | T | T | T | T | T |
| T | T | F | T | F | F | T | T |
| T | F | T | F | T | T | T | F |
| T | F | F | F | T | F | F | F |
| F | T | T | T | T | T | T | T |
| F | T | F | T | F | T | T | T |
| F | F | T | T | T | T | T | T |
| F | F | F | T | T | T | T | T |

Truth values in the last column are not same, hence it is contingency.

iv) \([(p \vee q) \vee r] \leftrightarrow [p \vee (q \vee r)]\)

| \(p\) | \(q\) | \(r\) | \(p \vee q\) | \((p \vee q) \vee r\) | \(q \vee r\) | \(p \vee (q \vee r)\) | \([(p \vee q) \vee r] \leftrightarrow [p \vee (q \vee r)]\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | T | T | T | T | T | T |
| T | T | F | T | T | T | T | T |
| T | F | T | T | T | T | T | T |
| T | F | F | T | T | F | T | T |
| F | T | T | T | T | T | T | T |
| F | T | F | T | T | T | T | T |
| F | F | T | F | T | T | T | T |
| F | F | F | F | F | F | F | T |

All the truth values in the last column are T, hence it is tautology.

subtopic: Quantifiers, Duality and Negation of Statements
context: If A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}, determine the truth value of the following.
solution:
For \(x = 7\), \(x - 4 = 7 - 4 = 3\)
\(\therefore x = 7\) satisfies the equation \(x - 4 = 3\)
\(\therefore\) The given statement is true and its truth value is T.

subtopic: Quantifiers, Duality and Negation of Statements
context: If A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}, determine the truth value of the following.
solution:
For \(x = 1\), \(x + 1 = 1 + 1 = 2\) which is not greater than or equal to 3
\(\therefore\) For \(x = 1\), \(x + 1 \geq 3\) is not true.
\(\therefore\) The truth value of given statement is F.

subtopic: Quantifiers, Duality and Negation of Statements
context: Write the negations of the following.
solution:
Let \(p : 3 + 3 < 5\); \(q : 5 + 5 = 9\)
Given statement is \(p \vee q\) and its negation is \(\sim(p \vee q)\) and \(\sim(p \vee q) \equiv \sim p \wedge \sim q\)
\(\therefore\) The negation of given statement is \(3 + 3 \geq 5\) and \(5 + 5 \neq 9\)

subtopic: Quantifiers, Duality and Negation of Statements
context: Write the negations of the following.
solution:
Let \(p : 7 > 3\); \(q : 4 > 11\)
The given statement is \(p \wedge q\)
Its negation is \(\sim(p \wedge q)\) and \(\sim(p \wedge q) \equiv \sim p \vee \sim q\)
\(\therefore\) The negation of given statement is \(7 \leq 3\) or \(4 \leq 11\)

subtopic: Quantifiers, Duality and Negation of Statements
context: Write the negations of the following.
stem: The number is neither odd nor perfect square.
solution:
Let \(p\) : The number is odd
\(q\) : The number is perfect square
Given statement can be written as 'the number is not odd and not perfect square'
Given statement is \(\sim p \wedge \sim q\)
Its negation is \(\sim(\sim p \wedge \sim q) \equiv p \vee q\)
The negation of given statement is 'The number is odd or perfect square'.

subtopic: Quantifiers, Duality and Negation of Statements
context: Write the negations of the following.
stem: The number is an even number if and only if it is divisible by 2.
solution:
Let \(p\) : The number is an even number.
\(q\) : The number is divisible by 2
Given statement is \(p \leftrightarrow q\)
Its negation is \(\sim(p \leftrightarrow q)\)
But \(\sim(p \leftrightarrow q) \equiv (p \wedge \sim q) \vee (q \wedge \sim p)\)
\(\therefore\) The negation of given statement is 'A number is even but not divisible by 2 or a number is divisible by 2 but not even'.

subtopic: Quantifiers, Duality and Negation of Statements
context: Write the converse, inverse and contrapositive of the following statements.
stem: If a function is differentiable then it is continuous.
solution:
Let \(p\) : A function is differentiable
\(q\) : A function is continuous.
\(\therefore\) Given statement is \(p \to q\)
i) Its converse is \(q \to p\)
If a function is continuous then it is differentiable.
ii) Its inverse is \(\sim p \to \sim q\).
If a function not differentiable then it is not continuous.
iii) Its contrapositive is \(\sim q \to \sim p\)
If a function is not continuous then it is not differentiable.

subtopic: Quantifiers, Duality and Negation of Statements
context: Write the converse, inverse and contrapositive of the following statements.
stem: If it rains then the match will be cancelled.
solution:
Let \(p\) : It rains, \(q\) : The match gets cancelled.
\(\therefore\) Given statement is \(p \to q\)
i) Its converse is \(q \to p\)
If the match gets cancelled then it rains.
ii) Inverse is \(\sim p \to \sim q\)
If it does not rain then the match will not be cancelled.
iii) Its contrapositive is \(\sim q \to \sim p\).
If the match is not cancelled then it does not rain.
